outlook.body:
- Expand the product portfolio, with emphasis on value-added and premium fabrics (premium shirting, functional textiles, fashion fabrics and customised textile solutions).
- Strengthen customer relationships and improve customer service, retaining a customer-centric operating model.
- Increase operational efficiencies and enhance manufacturing capabilities through continued investment in modern machinery and technological upgradation.
- Expand market presence across both domestic and international/export markets.
- Maintain product innovation and continuous product development as the response to changing fashion trends and consumer preferences.
- Use the BSE SME listing (effective 03.12.2025) to strengthen the corporate profile, improve access to capital and accelerate future growth plans.

outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The annual report describes no named expansion project, no new plant and no dated commissioning or ramp-up plan. Manufacturing remains concentrated at the single facility at Umbergaon, Gujarat, equipped with modern weaving technology including Sulzer Projectile, Picanol, Rapier and Electronic Dobby looms; management states that continuous investment in modern machinery enables the Company to maintain high standards of quality and productivity, and that investments in modern machinery, product development and market expansion are expected to support sustainable long-term growth. Growth strategy is framed as enhancing manufacturing capabilities and operational efficiency rather than as a capacity addition with a timeline. The capital commitments note states that the estimated amount of contracts remaining to be executed on capital account and not provided for (net of advances) is Nil, with a Nil prior-year comparative, indicating no contracted capex outstanding at the balance-sheet date.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Indian textile industry remains one of the largest contributors to manufacturing output, exports and employment; management calls the outlook positive.
- Rising domestic consumption, favourable demographics and increasing disposable incomes are expected to support demand.
- Increasing preference for branded apparel, growth in organised retail and expansion of e-commerce platforms are cited as demand drivers.
- Government initiatives - PM MITRA Parks, the PLI Scheme, National Technical Textiles Mission and 'Make in India' - are expected to provide long-term growth opportunities for the sector.
- The 'China Plus One' sourcing strategy adopted by several global buyers is creating opportunities for Indian textile manufacturers to expand international presence.
- Demand for premium fabrics and value-added products is expected to grow steadily; increasing demand for premium shirting fabrics, functional textiles, fashion fabrics and customised textile solutions gives room to broaden the offering.
- Performance is influenced by domestic and global textile/apparel demand, consumer spending, raw material prices, fashion trends, export demand, foreign exchange movements and textile-sector government policy.
- Headwinds flagged: raw material price volatility, changing market dynamics, global economic uncertainties, competitive pressure on pricing/margins/market share from large integrated players, unorganised manufacturers and imports.

sk.overview: India ranks as the 6th largest exporter of textiles and apparel globally, with the sector (including handicrafts) accounting for 8.21% of the country's total exports in 2023-24 and a 3.91% share of global textile and apparel trade (elsewhere cited as 4.6% of global trade and a 4.5% share ranking fifth in production). The USA and the European Union are the primary export destinations, together making up approximately 47% of India's textile and apparel exports. The industry contributes around 2.3% to GDP, 13% to industrial production and 10.5% to exports, directly employs over 45 million people (supporting more than 100 million indirectly), produces approximately 22 billion garments annually, and is currently valued at USD 174 billion with a projection to reach USD 350 billion by 2030 adding an estimated 35 million jobs. The sector faces headwinds from fluctuating cotton prices, weak demand in the US/EU export markets, rising freight costs and import competition from China and Bangladesh, but is supported by government schemes, growth in technical textiles and man-made fibres, and market diversification opportunities including anticipated FTAs with the EU and UK.

sk.structure: Value chain runs raw material (natural fibres: cotton, wool, silk, flax; synthetic fibres: polyester, nylon, acrylic) -> ginning -> spinning (fibre to yarn) -> weaving/knitting (yarn to fabric) -> dyeing, printing and finishing -> garment manufacturing. Key segments: Cotton (India is the leading producer, cultivating all four species and contributing ~23% of global cotton production), Wool (ninth-largest producer), Silk (second-largest producer), Man-Made Fibres (17% of India's textile exports; sixth-largest MMF textiles exporter globally) and Technical Textiles (applications across construction, agriculture, aerospace, automotive, healthcare, protective gear, home care). Domestic manufacturers face intensified competition from imported fabrics and garments from China and Bangladesh, exacerbated by under-invoicing. Organised vs unorganised split not disclosed in DRHP.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Indian textile industry remains one of the largest contributors to manufacturing output, exports and employment; management calls the outlook positive.
- Rising domestic consumption, favourable demographics and increasing disposable incomes are expected to support demand.
- Increasing preference for branded apparel, growth in organised retail and expansion of e-commerce platforms are cited as demand drivers.
- Government initiatives - PM MITRA Parks, the PLI Scheme, National Technical Textiles Mission and 'Make in India' - are expected to provide long-term growth opportunities for the sector.
- The 'China Plus One' sourcing strategy adopted by several global buyers is creating opportunities for Indian textile manufacturers to expand international presence.
- Demand for premium fabrics and value-added products is expected to grow steadily; increasing demand for premium shirting fabrics, functional textiles, fashion fabrics and customised textile solutions gives room to broaden the offering.
- Performance is influenced by domestic and global textile/apparel demand, consumer spending, raw material prices, fashion trends, export demand, foreign exchange movements and textile-sector government policy.
- Headwinds flagged: raw material price volatility, changing market dynamics, global economic uncertainties, competitive pressure on pricing/margins/market share from large integrated players, unorganised manufacturers and imports.

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Expand the product portfolio, with emphasis on value-added and premium fabrics (premium shirting, functional textiles, fashion fabrics and customised textile solutions).
- Strengthen customer relationships and improve customer service, retaining a customer-centric operating model.
- Increase operational efficiencies and enhance manufacturing capabilities through continued investment in modern machinery and technological upgradation.
- Expand market presence across both domestic and international/export markets.
- Maintain product innovation and continuous product development as the response to changing fashion trends and consumer preferences.
- Use the BSE SME listing (effective 03.12.2025) to strengthen the corporate profile, improve access to capital and accelerate future growth plans.
- Mitigate business risk through diversification across products and markets so no single product category or segment dominates.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The annual report describes no named expansion project, no new plant and no dated commissioning or ramp-up plan. Manufacturing remains concentrated at the single facility at Umbergaon, Gujarat, equipped with modern weaving technology including Sulzer Projectile, Picanol, Rapier and Electronic Dobby looms; management states that continuous investment in modern machinery enables the Company to maintain high standards of quality and productivity, and that investments in modern machinery, product development and market expansion are expected to support sustainable long-term growth. Growth strategy is framed as enhancing manufacturing capabilities and operational efficiency rather than as a capacity addition with a timeline. The capital commitments note states that the estimated amount of contracts remaining to be executed on capital account and not provided for (net of advances) is Nil, with a Nil prior-year comparative, indicating no contracted capex outstanding at the balance-sheet date.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Long-standing market presence since 1991 with a reputation built on consistent quality, innovative designs and timely deliveries
- Diversified product portfolio across shirting, bottom-weight, industrial fabrics and garments, reducing dependence on any single product category
- Modern manufacturing infrastructure with Sulzer Projectile, Picanol, Rapier and Electronic Dobby looms, backed by continuous investment in machinery
- Long-standing customer relationships and a customer-centric approach across domestic and export markets
- Ability to respond quickly to changing fashion trends through continuous product development
- Listing on the SME Platform of BSE (w.e.f. 03.12.2025) expected to strengthen the corporate profile and improve access to capital
